I'm not really sure myself. Voat is very open and welcoming to new ideas. More so than other internet places.

One thing I would say is that because it's so hard to get the 100 comment points needed to downvoat things, voat unfortunately seems to generate a lot more racist/dumb/bad stuff that hangs around. It's good to be able to see it and know it exists, but it makes the site seem much less reasonable than I'm sure it really is.

Limited upvoats encourage people to save them for what really matters. Things of true importance. But it also makes it very very hard to get to 20 or 100 comment points and makes it hard to guage popularity.

What do you think?

Edit: I just realized I forgot the ? in the title. Sorry.

Edit2: So the vibe I am getting is positive. The more I think about it the more I am inclined to agree. It makes for a positive, inclusive atmosphere free of vote manipulation. The upvoat limit is a little more upsetting than the downvoat restriction, but I think also reasonable. I wish there was some way everything could be perfect but that is not the nature of the universe.
How do you guys feel about limited upvoats/downvoats
It's good. It forces people to participate.
It also seems like it'd be a deterrent to brigading and troll accounts. I wouldn't mind seeing tiers with gradual limits to weed out or minimize the impact from those sorts of accounts.

This was a double edged sword for me. On my first day, I found myself commenting just to get CCP, when I really didn't have anything to add.

When I ran out of upvotes, I headed back to reddit for the rest of that day, since I couldn't participate.

Overall though, I think the downvotes limiting is a good idea.
It could also increase the amount of pointless comments.

Definitely a good thing. My original idea was that maybe it made it harder to see what people liked, but then I realized that doesn't really matter. What matters is what I like and by having a lot of people submitting a lot of stuff, which all appears at about the same popularity, I can find things much more easily than on, say, Reddit, where I'll only really see it if it has more than a few hundred upvotes.
In my heart I know its a great idea, but having my voats limited like this is very frustrating.
It's frustrating (I can't upvoat this comment, apparently), but the lack of variety (of both posts and opinions) is the main reason I left Reddit. This system seems to generate more variety.

Talk about it. I'm more of a lurker than an active contributor. Haven't been able to upvoat posts since two days now. It's frustrating.

Maybe Voat can introduce another parameter, a 'like' perhaps, which won't affect the visibility of the post and isn't limited.

A limit as in "You must have ___ comment contribution points" is good because it encourages people to participate and not just contribute negativity to the site. I think 100 is a little steep, that could easily take someone 70 comments, especially with the userbase of VOAT as limited as it is.

Limiting them as in "You can upvoat ___ posts/comments" would be problematic. Users would feel discouraged from using the site more, and even if it's based on readership numbers to negate that, content should rise or fall based upon its relevancy and quality, not whether or not viewers have an upvoat on hand.
I like it. Stops you from upvoting everything and downvoting anything you don't want to hear. Votes mean more.
I didn't comment on the other 20-or-so times this question has been asked (albeit worded differently), but I will this time. It's fine.

I'm fine with not giving out downvotes. Downvote isn't a way to tell people you disagree with their views, nor to bury a comment you disagree with. Unfortunately redditors do exactly this. Upvotes on the other hand, is too limited and I wish we could give out more of them. It encourages content creators and get an important message people need to see that may be buried in the sea of comments to the top.
The limit is incredibly low to what it could have been. I've been active for 4 days and I have a SCP of 346, a CCP of 260, and a total upvotes given of 292. The limit was literally nothing.

A good piece of advice is to just use the site. You find something you think is interesting? Post it where you believe it'll thrive. Actually get into the comments and participate. I am active in /v/askvoat and /v/introductions. I find posts that interest me and I comment throughout them.

I think its a good idea, but seems like people will make alts to counteract it. As for the racist stuff, I think that is due to there being less mods. What I really do like is the old school "see exactly how many downgoats and upvotes a comment/post is getting"

It's not really that hard to get to a 100 CCP, I was able to do this feat within a week hardly trying. If I was actually making an effort then I suppose that it would have only taken a couple of days max. And this was before any of the really major Reddit migrations. Although, I don't know what the situation is now due to the population of this site ballooning overnight. Or whether the system needs to be reviewed due to the glut of new accounts or what. IIRC they've already increased the number of up votes that you're able to use just after the Fattening exodus.

The logic behind voting limits is so you can't just make a bunch of alt accounts for the sole purpose down vote stuff that you happen to disagree with. This being something that happens on Reddit all the time. Sure it's not that much effort to reach the limit but it's enough of a barrier to stop the majority of trolls. I think due to it requiring actual effort.

Personally I would rather they not change it because it's this absolutely common sense stuff - like limiting the number of subs that you can mod, or not automatically subbing new accounts to a number of defaults - that helps to differentiate Voat from Reddit. If they were to remove these features due to user pressure to be (I speculate) more in line with what they've been conditioned to accept on Reddit then you might as well just go back to using Reddit, I'd argue.

I dislike that I am limited in my upvoating/downvoating ability. Voat is about freedom of expression and I feel that limiting the number of times I can upvoat something is debilitating and removes my freedom. That being said, people need to know how to use voating before they up/downvoat. Downvoating is not a "I don't like/agree with this" button, it's a "I don't think this positively contributes to the discussion at hand" button. Upvoating is the same, not a "I like/agree with this" but rather a "I believe this positively effects the discussion, contributes reliable information, and should be seen by more users" button.

If we were all able to follow these guidelines then the restrictions for up/downvoating should be removed. And really, come on guys, we can all live up to that.
